precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Soon as we give our life to the Lord, repent, and start to do the work, Satan comes before the throne and says, have you considered your servant such and such? They are doing well now, but let me try them and they will curse you, leave the truth, and go right back to me. And the Lord says, you can try, but do not take their life. You have got to understand the pattern, because it still operates today.
precepts.point: Then came the trials, one messenger on top of another. The Sabeans took the oxen and the asses and slew the servants: the first trial, dealing with his businesses and finances. The fire burned up the sheep and the servants: the second, again his business and finances. The Chaldeans made out three bands and carried away the camels: the third. Then a great wind smote the four corners of the house and his sons and daughters were dead: the fourth trial, dealing with Job's family.
precepts.why:
Satan said to the Lord about Job, “Doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” Job's life was blessed, and Satan brought it all out before the Lord: “But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.” Sirach shows that this is not only Job's story: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.”

As soon as we give our life to the Lord, the Lord forgives us of our sins, we repent, and we start to do the work. We get involved, we study, we clean our lives up according to the commandments. And while the Lord is sitting on the throne, Satan comes up and says, have you considered your servant such and such, or sister such and such? They've been doing real well. Yeah, they are doing good right now, but I guarantee you, if you let me do A, B or C to them, they are going to curse you. They are going to leave the truth, blaspheme your name, and go right back to me and white Jesus.

And the Lord says, all right, go ahead, you can try. Don't kill them; don't take their life. Just as he said to Satan about Job, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.”

Then came Job's trials, one messenger right on top of another. The Sabeans took the oxen and the asses and slew the servants: the first trial, his businesses and finances. The fire burned up the sheep and the servants: the second, his business and finances again. The Chaldeans carried away the camels: the third. Then a great wind smote the house and his sons and daughters were dead: the fourth, his family. That is what it means to prepare your soul for temptation. The pattern Job went through is the same one every servant who comes to the Lord goes through today.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. You are going to be tempted by Satan; he is going to use devices to tempt you. Set thy heart aright: get your mind right, get yourself together, because this is not going to be a fair fight. And constantly endure: you have to constantly endure these temptations, because you have things in you that you need to purge off, and some of these things keep coming back. That is why Paul in Romans 7 asked the Lord to take the thorn away, and the Lord said no, this is what you are going to have to battle. But on the flip side, dealing with those battles is what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with our life, how we communicate, how we deal in relationships, how we deal with one another. Make not haste in time of trouble: things are going to happen and you cannot fold up; you have to fight. Everybody is not going to make it victorious. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate: for gold is tried in the fire. You are going to be tried, so make sure you are on point.
precepts.point: And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death. It becomes action; that sin is the action you take after you have been enticed by your lust. And it always ends in destruction. That is why we have to be on point.
precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life.” You are going to be tried. Sirach tells you to get ready for it: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” You are going to be tempted by Satan; he is going to use devices to tempt you.

“Set thy heart aright”: get your damn mind right, get yourself together, because this is not going to be a fair fight, and it is not going to be easy. “and constantly endure”: you have to constantly endure these temptations, because you have demons in you that you need to purge off, and some of these things keep coming back, and you have to be able to fight and get away from them. Paul in Romans 7 asked the Lord to take it away, and the Lord said no, this is the thorn in your side; this is what you will have to battle. But on the flip side, dealing with those battles is what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with our lives, how we communicate, how we deal in relationships and with one another.

“and make not haste in time of trouble.” Things are going to happen, and you can’t fold up; go full-fledged toward it and knock it out. Life is a fight, and everybody is not going to make it victorious and on top. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. For gold is tried in the fire.”

You are going to be tried, so make sure you are on point. Everything in the world is against the person trying to be righteous: the work schedule set up to keep you in sin on the weekend, the holidays you want off based on wickedness. So you have to be around righteous people who will hold you accountable. That is the man who endures temptation and receives the crown of life.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.
precepts.point: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. It is going to happen; it is inevitable. Remember Ecclesiasticus 2: my son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. You caught hell coming into this truth; Satan did not want to let you go. Old acquaintances from years ago suddenly contacting you: Satan wanted you. He does not want one of us to wake up. But we are here.
precepts.why:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” It is just a part of being in this truth. All of you went through it; you don’t even have to be asked. You caught hell coming into this truth. That is just how it works.

Satan didn’t want to let you go. He didn’t want to give you up. You had family, you had old hoes contacting you from years ago: how did you get my number? Satan. Satan wanted you. He doesn’t want a single one of us to wake up. But we are here.

That is why Paul says “all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” It is going to happen; you are going to go through things; it is inevitable. “For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.” There are going to be schisms and divisions and things happening amongst us, all to find out who is built for the battle and who is going to make it through. Is a confrontation with a sister you keep bumping heads with going to take you out? Your marijuana addiction, your addiction to women, your addiction to porn? Or are you going to fight the fight and keep throwing blows back while you are getting hit? As long as you are fighting you are all right; the moment you stop fighting, it is over.

Pressure either bursts pipes or it doesn’t. Pressure exposes the weak points, and then you see where the repairs need to be made. And some go through heavy things, a husband who did this and that, and they are still here, strong as hell. Christ said “It is impossible but that offences will come.” Somebody is going to disappoint you, misunderstand you, correct you, overlook you, frustrate you. You didn’t run away from home over a fight with your sibling; you stayed, and you didn’t stop loving them. We are in the trenches, and we are not leaving. Prepare your soul for it, because the temptation is part of coming to serve the Lord.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Joseph understood this, because his father taught him. Make not haste in time of trouble: don't leave this truth in your time of trouble, because Satan will tell you that you had it better when you served him. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. Joseph's family was rich; Jacob was wealthy. Joseph was taken from all that, and now he's in the midst of poverty, in prison. Just as it goes for us, it went for our father Joseph.
precepts.point: His master's wrath was kindled, and Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound. Remember how old Joseph is: 17.
precepts.why:
Joseph was 17, falsely accused, and thrown into the king's prison. Sirach tells you why this should not shock a servant of God: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” Joseph understood this, because his father Jacob taught him.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” Make not haste means don't leave this truth in your time of trouble. Satan will tell you, if you weren't in that Bible you wouldn't be going through half of what you're going through; you had it better when you served me. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.”

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Joseph's family was rich; Jacob was a wealthy man. Joseph was taken from all that, sold as a slave, and now he is in the midst of poverty, in prison, for a crime he refused to commit. That is a low estate, and he bore it without leaving God.

Just as it goes for us, it went for our father Joseph. Israel today has been brought down to a low estate, and the tests and trials come because we serve the Lord. Endure them, cleave unto him, and you will be increased at your last end, as Joseph was.

precepts.text: Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy, and go not aside, lest ye fall. Believe him, and your reward shall not fail. Look at the generations of old, and see: did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? Was Job confounded? No. For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy, and saveth in time of affliction.
precepts.point: Only a spiritual man can understand that. Joseph was on another level of understanding: he sat back and reflected on all that happened to him and knew it was God's divine plan. He may not have understood it while he was in the midst of it, but going through the years of plenty and famine he realized his purpose, and God set that whole thing up.
precepts.why:
Sirach speaks to those in the middle of the trial: “Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall.” Don't go aside; don't say, I want to leave this truth and do something else. If you do, you will fall.

“Ye that fear the Lord, believe him; and your reward shall not fail.” “Ye that fear the Lord, hope for good, and for everlasting joy and mercy.”

“Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?” Was Job confounded? No. Was Joseph forsaken? No; what his brethren meant for evil, God meant for good. “For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saveth in time of affliction.”

That is the close of Joseph's story: wait on the Lord, go not aside, and he saves in the time of affliction.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. As you are preparing your soul, that is the Lord trying you to make sure you are worthy of that calling. It was already discussed in the heavens to bring you in; it is up to us to stay diligent and steadfast, and not get pulled off by sin, because we are a chosen vessel. You have to see yourselves that way.
precepts.point: Video played: the old United Negro College Fund commercial, "A mind is a terrible thing to waste." The mind of the Israelites, men and women, is a precious thing. For the Lord to call you out of darkness into his marvelous light is because you have a mind to do great things. We have known many brothers and sisters that came in with good gifts they could have dedicated to the Lord's nation, then got weak hearted, went back out into the world, and are doing nothing. This was the time to shine.

note.label: The Developmental Psychology of Being Hated

precepts.why:
The Lord is “not willing that any should perish”, so any one of us that comes into this truth, the desire is for you to make it. Peter says “give diligence to make your calling and election sure”. The Most High called you sisters and you brothers in here, and that was not a waste. It was made to happen in the heavens when it was time for you to wake up. Just as there was a conversation in the heavens about Job, when Satan wanted to tempt him, there were conversations about you repenting. That's some love right there. Understand that sacred calling.

Then Sirach: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” He wants to try you to make sure you are fit for the kingdom. But he first selected you. He brought you into his marvellous gospel to wake you up and bring you up as princes and princesses; no longer are you to be on the dunghill. As you prepare your soul for temptation, that is the Lord trying you to make sure you are worthy of that calling.

It was already discussed in the heavens to bring you in, so it is up to us to stay diligent and steadfast, and not get pulled off by evil, wickedness, sin, temptations and the things our people get caught up in. We are a chosen vessel, and you have to see yourselves that way.

Peter goes on, “for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”: that is the guarantee of keeping God's commandments. So why squander the chance Christ died to give you because of some bad habits and temptations? Every one of your spirits is precious to the Most High, and it hurts leadership to see you get weak and lose the faith. A mind is a terrible thing to waste. Many brothers and sisters came in with good gifts, got weak hearted, went back out, and are doing nothing. This was the time to shine.

precepts.text: Gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. You are that gold; some of you want to be iron or silver. Gold is purified in the fire, and if you will not let the unclean be purged out you cannot have the kingdom. Esau has put you through hell all your life; do not lose the kingdom on top of it by holding on to things from five, twenty, or fifty years ago like a woman bringing up the pineapple when you are talking about the orange. It takes a strong man to take correction; when correction comes, push harder to prove to Messiah you are still in the fight.
precepts.point: Some of you will betray the brother next to you out of fear, because Esau threatens to tell the congregation what you were watching; your mind was in porn instead of the scriptures. With AI they will set many of us up with fake video, and some of our own people will believe it with no proof because they never built their minds in the scriptures.
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” You are that gold. We are that gold. How do you purify gold? By putting it in the fire. Some of you need to go into the fire. You have stuff on you that has to be purged out, but you want to keep it and still have the kingdom of heaven. If you don't want to be purged, you cannot get the kingdom. Some of you want to be iron, some of you want to be silver; you have to be that gold.

What is the purpose of going through all that and not getting the kingdom? Esau has been putting you through hell all your life, and you end up missing the kingdom because you hold on to things and don't want God to take the unclean out of you.

Some of you hold on to things that happened fifty years ago, twenty years ago, five years ago. That's like a woman in an argument: you're talking about the orange and she says, yeah, but the pineapple happened five years ago. There's no pineapple here; we're talking about the orange. Some sisters got notes, waiting to bring them out. Men should not be emotional like that.

And “acceptable men in the furnace of adversity”: it takes a strong man to take correction. Weak men cannot. When correction comes, the strong man gets up, repents and keeps moving, and you can tell he is still in the fight. When you get correction, that's when you push harder. Don't lay back. Prove to Messiah, not to leadership, that you are still in the fight.

precepts.text: They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts and humble their souls in his sight. War is imminent and the birthing pains will get worse; prepare your mind so that whatever evil comes you remain faithful, and rejoice, because the scriptures said it would happen.
precepts.point: Ezra had prepared his heart, his mind, to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. We are in captivity, working and tired, and the Most High reminds us these are the last days, so prepare your mind.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Why prepare our minds and our spirits? Because war is imminent. We are seeing Iran and Israel at war and America getting involved, and the wars are only going to get worse. What we see right now is a birthing pain. Yet all of us are supposed to rejoice, because the scriptures already told us this was going to happen.

Sirach says: “They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight”. All of us that fear the Lord will prepare our minds, so that whatever evil comes upon the earth, we will remain faithful in serving the Lord.

That is Ezra's example: a heart prepared, and a soul humbled in the Lord's sight, ready to seek the law, do it, and teach it, whatever comes.

precepts.text: Gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. The same fire that destroys some men purifies the acceptable ones. When the ADL and government organizations attack, some will leave and some will come out pure gold.
precepts.point: Even the worst things, like Job losing his kids, are to make us perfect. It is a hard saying, but without Satan our adversary we cannot become perfect.
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” That fire, the furnace of adversity, is temptation. Adversity comes from our adversary, and our adversary is that spiritual demon and his children. So the furnace of adversity in Sirach is the work of the adversary the devil in Peter.

Acceptable men are that gold. When an acceptable man goes through that fire, it doesn't destroy him. It makes him better; it purifies him. When Satan attacks and kills and puts in prison, some men it will destroy, and some men it will make perfect in the sight of God. When the ADL and all these governmental organizations attack us, some of you sisters will be up out of here: I ain't messing with them, the government say they a hate group. Some of you brothers will be gone too. But some of you will be purified and become that pure gold.

You have to go through adversity. Your enemy has to attack you; that is how you become better and how you become a better fighter. Then Peter's words come to pass: “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.” Nobody wants to suffer, but the Lord says if you want the kingdom you have to suffer, and if you are acceptable, after you suffer you will get the kingdom. Suffering makes you perfect, establishes you, strengthens you until you are battle hardened like somebody who has been warring for thirty or forty years, and settles you within your spirit: it is what it is.

precepts.text: They that fear the Lord will not disobey His word; Abraham's fear was proved by his obedience.
precepts.point: Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.
precepts.why:
“Now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.” How was the fear of God known? By obedience. “They that fear the Lord will not disobey his Word; and they that love him will keep his ways.”

Abraham bound Isaac, laid him on the altar and stretched forth his hand with the knife before the angel called out of heaven, “Lay not thine hand upon the lad.” The fear of God is proved in obedience, and Abraham’s fear was proved right there on the altar. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.

precepts.text: Cleave unto Him and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end; hold on until the blessing.
precepts.point: That is the spirit to carry through hardship: fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life the way Jacob laid hold and would not let go.
precepts.why:
“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.”

Jacob is the picture of it. A man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day and had to put the hollow of his thigh out of joint, because Jacob would not be beaten. Even then he held on: “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.” That is faith with works: cleaving to the Most High and not departing, thigh out of joint, until he was increased at his last end with the blessing.

precepts.text: Prepare thy soul for temptation and constantly endure; Joseph was gold tried in the fire.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” These are the characteristics of Joseph. He was tempted in Potiphar’s house and endured; he was put in prison and made not haste in the time of trouble. Do not be quick to leave the truth or find excuses in the time of trouble.

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Joseph was changed to a low estate, sold and imprisoned, and he was increased at his last end, governor over all the land of Egypt.

“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. Believe in him, and he will help thee; order thy way aright, and trust in him.” Joseph was gold tried in the fire, and the Lord helped him.

precepts.text: Saul made haste in a time of trouble; he panicked and did unadvisedly, and he is going to suffer consequences for it.
precepts.point: Brothers do the same thing today: leadership said it would be here at ten, it is five past ten, so we cancel the plan and go home. Be humble and tarry like you were instructed; it may run some minutes over, and the Lord may be testing your patience.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
Samuel had instructed Saul in chapter 10: when you get to Gilgal, tarry seven days, make no moves until I arrive. Saul “tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.” The people were acting frantic, and Saul said, “Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.” Saul is not the priest; that is Samuel’s office.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” Saul made haste in a time of trouble. He panicked and did unadvisedly, and he is going to suffer consequences for it. Then, “as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came”: he was barely late, and Saul could not hold his patience.

Brothers do the same thing today: leadership said it would be here at ten, it is five past ten, so we cancel the plan and go home. Be humble and tarry like you were instructed. It may run some minutes over, and the Lord may be testing your patience.

precepts.text: If you abide in the fear of God you will not be forsaken.
precepts.point: I cry in the daytime but thou hearest not, but thou art holy; our fathers trusted in thee and thou didst deliver them; they cried unto thee and were delivered.

note.label: Psalm 22: The Prophecy of Christ on the Cross

precepts.why:
“Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them. They cried unto thee, and were delivered: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.” Ecclesiasticus points to the same fathers: “Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?”

Look at the generations of old. Nobody who trusted in the Lord was confounded, nobody who abided in his fear was forsaken, and nobody who called on him was despised. If you abide in the fear of God, you will not be forsaken. Even crying in the daytime and in the night season, he is holy, and the fathers who trusted him were delivered.

precepts.text: Believe in Him and He will help you; stipulations to His help. The fearful heart and the sinner that goeth two ways cannot serve both; the fainthearted who believes not shall not be defended.
precepts.point: Wait on the Most High and be of good courage, and He shall strengthen your heart. But the double-minded, half in and half out, He will not defend, and this comes up again in the later chapters.

note.label: Psalm 27: The Most High Is My Light and Salvation

precepts.why:
“I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living. Wait on the Lord: be of good courage”. Every line reads like a stipulation, and Ecclesiasticus lays the stipulations out: “Believe in him, and he will help thee; order thy way aright, and trust in him. Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall. Ye that fear the Lord, believe him; and your reward shall not fail.”

Believe in Him and He will help you; those are stipulations to His help. “Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?” Without faith that the kingdom is coming, David would have fainted, but he believed to see the goodness of the Lord.

Then the warning: “Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goeth two ways! Woe unto him that is fainthearted! for he believeth not; therefore shall he not be defended.” The fearful heart and the sinner that goeth two ways cannot serve both. The double-minded, half in and half out, He will not defend, and this comes up again in the later chapters. Wait on the Most High, be of good courage, and He shall strengthen your heart, even with false witnesses and such as breathe out cruelty risen up against you.

precepts.text: If you come to serve the Most High, prepare your soul, set your heart right, endure, and take whatever is brought upon you cheerfully, staying patient when changed to a lower state.
precepts.point: In my prosperity I said I shall never be moved: the key point of making the Most High your refuge and salvation is staying on the right path regardless, whether prosperity or affliction comes.

note.label: Psalm 30: Joy Cometh in the Morning

precepts.why:
Prosperity says, I shall never be moved, but the one who serves the Most High is told to get ready: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.”

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” If you come to serve the Most High, prepare your soul, set your heart right, endure, and take whatever is brought upon you cheerfully, staying patient when changed to a lower state. That is staying on the right path regardless, whether prosperity or affliction comes.

precepts.text: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation, set thy heart aright, endure, and take whatever is brought upon thee cheerfully, for gold is tried in the fire and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
precepts.point: The Lord has chastened me sore but has not given me over unto death. When you come to serve the Lord, understand that this walk brings chastising to try us.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“The Lord hath chastened me sore: but he hath not given me over unto death.” When you come to serve the Lord, understand that this walk brings chastising to try us. “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.”

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Whatever is brought upon you, take it cheerfully.

“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” The chastening is the furnace; it tries us as gold is tried, and it does not give us over unto death. So the righteous can still say, I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the Lord.

precepts.text: Set thy heart aright and constantly endure the trials that will come.
precepts.point: Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” The Lord trieth the hearts, so the one who comes to serve him must prepare his soul for it: set thy heart aright and constantly endure the trials that will come.

That is the furnace of Proverbs 17. We must go through trials and tribulations to gain the kingdom, not merely accept Jesus in the heart and be saved forever, as Christianity falsely teaches.

precepts.text: We must be proven through trials to gain the kingdom.
precepts.point: Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” That is the furnace for gold of Proverbs 17 applied to us: as gold is tried in the fire, acceptable men are tried in the furnace of adversity.

The Most High tries our hearts through trials to rid us of our impurities. We must be proven through trials to gain the kingdom.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why:
This deals with what Deacon Malachi just said about the fearful; in case you think he was talking off the top of his head, it is scripture. “Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands,” Woe meaning destruction be to fearful hearts and faint hands: you don't want to do the work. “and the sinner that goeth two ways!” Because you are double-minded; you go two ways, one foot in the world, one foot in Israel. Double-minded also goes into you traitors sitting amongst us learning and taking notes at last night's class while harbouring evil; your mind ain't here, it is somewhere else. The traitors that leave this truth will be on YouTube teaching what we taught them, as if the spirit came upon them and they learned it by osmosis.

“Woe unto him that is fainthearted!” The fainthearted is the fearful brother, the fearful sister. “for he believeth not;” Because you don't believe. “therefore shall he not be defended.” God says he won't defend a brother or sister like that. That is some heavy stuff right there. How would you show your belief? By your works; your works show you believe. They work together. If anything is able to move you, that means you have not believed what we preach, what God is trying to let us know: these little trials and tribulations we are going through are to purify us, just like gold, just like silver. This war is not going to be easy; God did not make it easy. You have to have faith in this, apply it, live it. Everything happens for a reason, and these scriptures are to guide us, build us up, uplift us, but a lot of times brothers and sisters don't believe; that is your unbelief.

“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” We usually explain it for the individual, but it extends from the individual to a marriage to a congregation: the three trials of faith. The most common temptations for an individual are sex and money.

The Matrix shows it: the woman in the red dress, and the brother lost focus; sex is how brothers get hemmed up. And Cypher, who wanted to be rich and to be someone important, and betrayed Morpheus, his brothers, for it. The love of money was the root of a lot of the foolishness: my business, my money, my hustle. Write it down, sex and money, because it ain’t the end; it is going to continue.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: The fearful. “Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goeth two ways!”: you’re double-minded. You got the Bible in your hand, but you won’t do nothing it says.

note.label: The Decayed State of Liberal Women

points: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Because Satan is not just going to allow you to wake up and wake up God's people. He is not going to stand by while you are out here teaching, out here prophesying. We have to prepare our souls for temptations, because things are going to happen that will hinder you in this truth.

Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble. We have to set our hearts right, because out of this wicked mind comes all manner of wickedness. And we have to constantly endure in this truth, and that comes with studying, praying and applying. Leadership tells us this all the time. And when those temptations come, do not make haste. We have to endure.

My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. Everybody in here came to serve the Lord, right? Then bad things are going to happen in your life. Why? Because he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: your adversary the devil is coming for you, and he is coming hard.

Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble. When Satan comes and bad things happen, keep enduring. Do not make haste: some of you sisters go through problems in your marriage and want to up and leave. Trouble and affliction come through your spouse and your marriage too; do not make haste. Unless there is real danger or abuse and you have to separate for a time, when things get bad you should not give up or walk out. Things get serious and some of you say, I am out; that is fake and phony, and the Lord is showing who is fake and phony, who loves him and who does not.

Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Cleave unto the Lord when you are going through bad things: when you are sick, when your child is sick, when you lost your house, when you are in prison. When you are by yourself, it is only you and the Lord; learn to cleave to him and talk to him. In the end of everything, you are going to increase. Brothers went through the fire and lost everything, and the Most High blessed them; they increased in the end.
Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. Sometimes we are going to be brought very low, but we must be patient.

For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. To be acceptable means to be chosen. The same way gold is tried in fire, if you are acceptable, God puts you through adversity: tribulation, persecution, sickness. The way Job went through it. Every son that he chooses, he chastens; and the reason he puts us through these things is to make us perfect.
Believe in him, and he will help thee; order thy way aright, and trust in him. Did it say trust in Malachiah? Trust in God. Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall.
My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation: that is the qualifier. When you sign up to do the Lord's work, now you are in the furnace; now the fire turns on.

Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure: because the fire never turns off. The impurities never stop; you are constantly being bombarded, constantly pressured to do the wrong thing. Look at social media; look at how the world is being turned upside down. Everything that is wrong in the earth right now is because the people over the earth are wicked. So if you find yourself at rest, that means you are not being purged; you are off the stove, you are cold; matter of fact, you are in the refrigerator.

Make not haste in time of trouble: the fire has to stay on you to burn the impurities out. If you make haste and leave, you cool down and go back to the state you were in. And once you turn your back to him, who is going to turn the fire back on? Satan makes it easy for you; Satan gives you your heart's desire, everything you want. You want your coworker, you can have him; you like watching porn, here is your whole algorithm. The restraint is the fire: putting the phone down, putting blocks on the phone, throwing the phone in the trash if it got too bad for you. The fire is the restraint, turning away from evil.

Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. A brother answered what the increase at the last end is: getting the kingdom. That is why we go through this; the fire has a reason, the restraint has a reason. You have to go through this to get to the next level. There is no neutral gear; either you are moving forward or you are moving backwards, either you are hot and fervent or you are ice cold. Christ said pick one; if you are in the middle, you are going to die.

Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully: whatever trial comes, take it cheerfully, because the trials have to come to purge it out of you. You go through trials and it feels like your family is against you; do you turn back, go eat the ham sandwich and open the Christmas gifts? Do you give up ten or fifteen years in this truth because you lost your job, so your family can welcome you back with open arms? When you give up on the brothers and sisters that labor in this truth with you, where are you going back to, and what is waiting for you when you get there? Absolutely nothing. Putting the ball down is easy; walking on and laboring with your brothers is the hard part, because we labor together.

For gold is tried in the fire. It is not just something burning; it is something being purged, being tried, being cleaned. Fire is a purifier, one of the best purifiers, and the Most High uses fire all through the Bible to purify, because it burns out the impurities, the bad elements, the things that will corrupt you. If he did not use the fire, you would not get cleaned. The metalworkers do the same thing: they heat up the elements to burn out the impurities and get the best element. That is us. To get the best you, the impurities have to be burned out.
My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. It comes from every side: cigarettes, crack, the big-butt woman, the men. Never think you stand and cannot fall, or you will.

Set thy heart aright; it is all about your mind. Constantly endure means keep fighting, do not give up, and watch for the devil, who only needs a little crack in the door to fit himself in. Make not haste in time of trouble: when correction comes, do not run; take it, repent, and keep moving.

If you have come into this truth and you are serving the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation — and that temptation is going to come from the people who so-called love you, the people you grew up with, the people who raised you.

Constantly endure: do not let them pull you and make you feel bad for not coming.

note.label: Black Christians Stuck in Delusional Orbiting Cycles of Stupidity

points: My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. So the Most High is always preparing us. Prepare yourself, because you are going to be tempted. You are going to be tempted, it is what it is, there is no getting around it. You are going to get tempted when you want to come and serve God, when you want to do right, keep the commandments, live righteously. Things are going to come your way.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: Set thy heart aright. Get your mind right, because if your mind is not right for this truth — it is a shock, the things that you find out you are supposed to be keeping. You are like, this sounds like a lot, but really it is everyday living that we need to do. It is just the right thing we need to be doing. You have got to get your mind right for the change, because if not you are going to start bugging out.

And constantly endure. Why constantly endure? Because it is going to happen over and over. It is not about if something is going to happen to you, or if you are going to get tried — it is when. When will you be tried. You might come in and everything is smooth sailing for five, six years, and that seventh year is the worst year you ever had in your life. Things are happening, you are losing jobs, you are losing your car. You are in the house, your car is in the driveway, you come outside and it is gone. You have not made payments in about six months. The repo man pulled up and hooked that thing up, beep beep beep, early in the morning. You come out thinking you are about to go to the Sabbath and your car is gone, and you have got the kids with you, and now you are about to lose your job because you have no way to get to work.

And make not haste in time of trouble. So when things get rough, do not run away. Do not be like, hey listen man, I cannot do this truth any more, I am going through it, it is too much, I cannot bear it. Brothers and sisters be running away from what they are dealing with. Running away is going to make it worse. The Most High wants you to call on him when things are rough. That is where your faith comes in. You have got to call on the Most High God, let him know what you are dealing with, ask him to reveal what you need to fix.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: Cleave unto him, and depart not away. So you have got to cleave unto the Most High when you are in these hard, trying days. Especially you new people — it is paramount that you cleave to the Most High, because these are like the golden years. When you come in you are fresh, but everything is against you: your family, your friends, your parents, your job.

You used to dress a little provocative at work, and one day they see you with fringes, hair wrapped, long skirt, and the first thing they say is, you Muslim now? You used to have your nice earrings, you were decked out, you had weave hanging halfway down your back, and you came in modest, and they are like, what is going on? And guess what, they start going into your Facebook seeing what you are about — your employers, your supervisors. That is how they do us. They know everything about you at work, and they can come against you.

That thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Because when we go through this, we go through this change. This is an upgrade. What did Beyonce say — upgrade you? This is the real upgrade right here, when you change your life for the better by keeping the commandments. This is the upgrade.

We all are being purified. We go through things to purify us. We are changing for the better, we are trying to be a more and more righteous example. Because what? The kingdom is at the end of the tunnel. We are the light of the world, we have got to show it.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully. So when things happen to us, take it cheerfully. Why? Because we know the Most High God is trying to purge something out of us. The Most High God is trying to fix us. We have got to take that cheerfully. The Most High is still dealing with me — that is how we all should look at it. He has not killed me, so I still have got a chance to get my stuff in order. So you have got to think, you know what, I am going to take this cheerfully. I am not going to pout about it, I am going to take it like a man, I am going to take it like a woman, and we are going to get through this.

I cannot let it overtake how I deal with people. I cannot let it overtake how I conduct my relationships with my brothers and my sisters and with my kids. You are going through something and you come home and you dog out your wife, you are beating the kids because you are going through something — no, that is not how you do it. You deal with it accordingly, like a righteous brother or sister. That is what you are supposed to be doing.

And be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. So when we are at a low state, be patient, because the Most High is going to get you back right. You have just got to believe that and understand: listen, this is a trial, we are going to get through this. Let us be movers and shakers, let us not sit on our behind and soak.

Let me examine myself. Self-examination is key in this truth. Every day you should be doing it, every day you should be working on yourself — whether it is in the truth, whether it is your career, whether it is your relationship with your wife, your relationship with your kids. Every day you have got to sit back and say, what can I do to get better in life? Because if your personal life is trash, you are going to be trashing the truth. Straight up. There is no super-duper Israelite who goes home to a house that is trash and has nothing in order. That does not make sense, it does not work like that.

If you are not getting your life together you are going to be trashing the truth. This is what I mean by when you are going through things: you come to the truth and everybody can see everything on you, everybody can see the disparity, the burning on you. It is not supposed to be like that. You should be developing your life. If you are unhappy with your income or whatever is going on, change it, better yourself. And when you are bettering yourself you are going to get better in the truth, because that is self-development. You are getting your mind clear.

So we have got to fix ourselves all around, in our personal life, in righteousness, and when it comes to the body. And we have the ability to do so. Why? Because God gave us the commandments. He gave us the blueprint, he gave us the law, statutes and commandments, he gave us Christ to be our saviour, to die for us so we can get our stuff together.

And it is not only you. When you are going through stuff and you are married, your spouse goes through it too. They are the ones that are there with you going through those things. How are you going to be going through something and go home and treat your wife like crap, or treat your husband like crap, when those are the people you sleep beside every night? You are going through financial issues together, you are going through health problems together. You should be taking this cheerfully together. Do not bring your issues down on everybody in the household, so that they say, oh my God, daddy just needs to get out of the house because he is tripping for no reason. Same thing for the wife. Your woman comes in after work, she is not cooking anything, she is bugging out, she is screaming at everybody, and you are looking at your wife like, I did not want to deal with you right now. That is not how we should be. As we are getting our families in order, we should be going through the same things with each other. We have got to make sure we are on the same page.

note.label: SABBATH MORNING CLASS: If Thou Come to Serve the Lord

points: For gold is tried in the fire. Gold is tried in the fire. Go look at somebody making a gold chain, melting gold, and see the work that goes into it. See the work that is being put into the gold to get it to where you can go and buy it and wear it. Back then you were building things with it; when you had money you had some dope stuff made out of gold. But it has got to go through something, it has got to go in and purify itself.

And acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. Remember, we are comparable to fine gold. Acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. So we have got to be purified, we have got to get all the impurities out. That is why we go through stuff. That is why Sirach 2 is saying, listen, when you are going through stuff do not run away from it. Deal with it, and cleave unto me, because I am trying to purge something out of you, I am trying to purify you, so you can be that fine gold, so you can be that light of the world, that light to the nation. That is what the Most High God is trying to do to us today, and you have got to understand that.

There are levels to this truth. As we grow in understanding, as we grow in the years, we start going into different levels, and then we start going into different levels of things we need to purge out. It does not get easier, it gets harder — you just get better at dealing with situations. That is the difference between when you come in as a babe and when you are an adolescent. It is a big difference in growth. You deal with things a lot differently.

You have got the bishops and the deacons, twenty-plus years, grown men in the truth, and you are not going to listen to what they are telling you? Every Sabbath, sometimes we go over deep stuff, but the bishops and the deacons are always trying to fix us. That is why I made the video yesterday: how dare somebody come in and dog men or women that are trying to get the man and woman in order. When you come against that, you are coming against God, you are coming against the Israelites, against IUIC, because we are trying to change all of that. We are trying to get the black man and black woman, the Hispanic man and woman, the Native American man and woman back in order, in their rightful place. We are holding up time right now. You always say, oh listen, I wish Christ would come — well, put in the work. We have got work to do. We have got to go get our people back, people have got to repent, and you have got to be that example.
